abstract: Multi-task learning (MTL) has emerged as a promising approach for deploying deep learning models in real-life applications. Recent studies have proposed optimization-based learning paradigms to establish task-shared representations in MTL. However, our paper empirically argues that these studies, specifically gradient-based ones, primarily emphasize the conflict issue while neglecting the potentially more significant impact of imbalance/dominance in MTL. In line with this perspective, we enhance the existing baseline method by injecting imbalance-sensitivity through the imposition of constraints on the projected norms. To demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed IMbalance-sensitive Gradient (IMGrad) descent method, we evaluate it on multiple mainstream MTL benchmarks, encompassing supervised learning tasks as well as reinforcement learning. The experimental results consistently demonstrate competitive performance.

bibliographic.title: Injecting Imbalance Sensitivity for Multi-Task Learning
bibliographic.venue: Proceedings of the Thirty-Fourth International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI-25)

content.problem: Gradient-based optimization methods for multi-task learning concentrate on resolving conflicting task gradients while neglecting the imbalance or dominance among individual task gradients, which the authors argue is the more significant obstacle to optimizing all tasks simultaneously.
content.proposed_solution: The authors inject imbalance sensitivity into an established gradient-combination baseline (CAGrad) by adding a projected-norm constraint that encourages the combined gradient to promote every individual task, with an adaptive weighting tied to a cosine-based measure of gradient imbalance, and apply the same idea to augment Nash-MTL.

content.claim: Adding imbalance sensitivity lets IMGrad consistently improve its gradient-manipulation baselines and surpass prior state-of-the-art gradient manipulation methods across supervised and reinforcement learning benchmarks, including the best overall ∆m% on NYUv2 and CityScapes and the highest success rate on MT10.
